summary: Luffy and his Straw Hat crew sail the Grand Line to become Pirate King, bound by friendship and dreams, fighting tyrants and freeing islands along the way.

hunger.why: Luffy's bottomless appetite, Sanji's cooking, feasts after every victory, and Sanji's vow never to refuse food to the hungry run throughout.

thirst.why: The Alabasta desert, with dried-up Yuba and the fight over water, makes thirst a real ordeal in one arc.

feeling-cold-hot.why: Drum Island's snow, Alabasta's desert heat, and Punk Hazard's burning and frozen halves are recurring hardships.

sleepiness.why: Zoro's constant naps and Luffy sleeping through danger are running gags; fatigue after battle recurs.

curiosity.why: Every arc lands on a new island: Skypiea in the clouds, Fish-Man Island, Wano; exploring the Grand Line is the premise.

explanation-seeking.why: Robin hunts the Poneglyphs and the Void Century, and the nature of the One Piece and the Will of D are long mysteries.

skill-acquisition.why: Luffy's Gears and Haki, Zoro's quest to be the greatest swordsman, and the two-year training timeskip make growth constant.

play.why: The crew's parties, games, pranks, and Luffy's goofing with Usopp and Chopper fill the quiet stretches.

resource-accumulation.why: Nami's hunger for treasure, rising bounties, and the legendary One Piece itself keep wealth in view.

resource-foraging.why: The crew forages for food, supplies, Log Poses, and cola for Franky on island after island.

mental-time-travel.why: Long flashbacks to each character's past and battle plans for Alabasta, Enies Lobby, and Wano shape the story.

fear-of-predators.why: Sea Kings, giant beasts, Thriller Bark's monsters, and Kaido's beast pirates menace the crew repeatedly.

fear-of-aggressors.why: Battles against rival pirates, Marines, Warlords, and Emperors are the core of every arc.

fear-of-heights.why: The Knock-Up Stream, Skypiea's cloud islands, and falls from Zou and Onigashima involve heights.

disgust.why: Thriller Bark's zombies, Magellan's poison, Caesar's gas, and the slave market at Sabaody evoke revulsion.

pain-aversion.why: Zoro absorbs Luffy's pain at Thriller Bark, Luffy is beaten at Marineford, Ace is impaled; wounds are relentless.

pride.why: Declaring dreams, becoming Pirate King, rising bounties, and the pride of the Straw Hat flag define every character.

shame.why: Usopp leaves the crew after losing, and the crew's helplessness at Sabaody and Luffy's failure at Marineford shame them into training.

moral-pride.why: Zoro's code, Luffy's refusal to abandon a friend, and Sanji's rules about women and the hungry are principles held at any cost.

guilt.why: Luffy blames himself for Ace's death, Robin for Ohara, Nami for her years with Arlong, Usopp for his betrayal.

warmth.why: Luffy's open-hearted kindness to strangers, Chopper's care, and the crew's tenderness for each other pervade the series.

moral-blame.why: The World Government's corruption, slavery at Sabaody, and every arc's tyrant are condemned by the crew.

moral-praise.why: Freed islands hail Luffy as a hero, and allies celebrate the crew's deeds across the seas.

revenge.why: Luffy avenges Nami against Arlong, Vivi's kingdom against Crocodile, and Law's past against Doflamingo.

forgiveness.why: Usopp is taken back after apologizing, Robin is forgiven her betrayal, and old enemies become allies.

compassion.why: Protecting the weak, from Nami's village to Dressrosa's toys and Wano's starving people, structures every arc.

affiliation.why: Luffy recruits crewmates one by one and befriends allies on every island, building a Grand Fleet.

friendship.why: Nakama, the bond among the Straw Hats, is the series' central value.

sadness.why: Ace's death, the Going Merry's funeral, and tragic backstories for Chopper, Robin, Brook, and Sanji bring tears in every arc.

humor.why: Gag faces, Luffy's idiocy, Sanji's nosebleeds, Zoro getting lost, and absurd villains make it a comedy throughout.

embarrassment.why: Sanji's humiliations, Usopp's cowardice exposed, and comic mishaps recur.

reasoning.why: Robin's historical deductions and negotiations with allies occur, but debates are secondary to action.

coalitional-affiliation.why: The Straw Hat crew, pirate alliances, Marines, Emperors' fleets, and the Grand Fleet make group identity everything.

status-seeking.why: Becoming Pirate King, bounties, Warlord and Emperor titles, and rankings of strength drive the whole world.

envy.why: Blackbeard covets others' powers and Bellamy mocks dreamers; envy is secondary.

anger.why: Luffy's rage when friends are hurt, at Arlong, Crocodile, and Akainu, drives his fiercest fights.

hatred.why: Arlong's and Hody's hatred of humans, Doflamingo's cruelty, and Akainu's contempt for pirates fuel villainy.

romantic-affiliation.why: Boa Hancock's devotion to Luffy and Sanji's crushes appear, but romance is marginal.

sexual-attraction.why: Sanji's lechery, Brook's requests, and Nami and Robin's fanservice are running gags.

long-term-love.why: Hancock's steadfast love, Oden and Toki, and Bell-mere's household show lasting commitment, briefly.

desire.why: Sanji's constant lust and Brook's panty jokes are comic, not plot.

romantic-jealousy.why: Sanji's jealousy over Nami and Hancock's possessiveness are played for laughs.

sexual-disgust.why: Absalom's attempt to force a wedding on Nami and Big Mom's forced marriage of Sanji are coercive.

parental-care.why: Bell-mere dies protecting Nami and Nojiko, Whitebeard shelters his sons, and Garp and Dadan raise Luffy.

parental-investment.why: Zeff raises Sanji, Hiriluk nurtures Chopper, Garp and Rayleigh train Luffy, and Oden mentors his retainers.

familial-love.why: Luffy, Ace, and Sabo as sworn brothers, Whitebeard's family, Nami and Bell-mere, and Sanji's Vinsmokes make kinship central.
